text:
alex: FYI a partner reported our Python onboarding async example failing on Windows across 3.8-3.12. Error trace shows CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED only when using AsyncClient. Sync example with requests is fine.

hana: Are they using the MS store build? That changes how OpenSSL and cert stores behave.

alex: They said python.org installer on Win11. certifi present.

tariq: Common pattern: httpx/anyio + Windows proactor loop sometimes causes socket/ssl weirdness. Also env vars like REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE are honored by requests but not always by async backends.

maria: Repro from my VM: AsyncClient -> ConnectionError, inner cause is ssl.SSLCertVerificationError. Our retry middleware was re-raising without chaining the original, so users only saw ConnectionError.

hana: Oof. Short fixes: 1) preserve __cause__ when re-raising in retry logic, 2) accept an ssl: Optional[ssl.SSLContext] on AsyncClient and document it, 3) update Windows sample to show certifi.where() fallback + selector loop.

tariq: Example snippet that helped me locally:
```python
import ssl, certifi, asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient

ssl_ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile=certifi.where())
asyncio.set_event_loop_policy(asyncio.WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy())

async def main():
    async with AsyncClient(ssl=ssl_ctx) as c:
        print(await c.generate("hi"))

asyncio.run(main())
```

maria: Also file bug: our type stubs don't list `ssl` on AsyncClient, so mypy users tried `verify=` which fails. I'll open a typing PR.

hana: CI request: add a lightweight Windows job for py3.8-3.12 to catch these regressions early. Platform team: can we add a small GH Actions runner matrix? @platform (tagging in channel).

alex: Created issue 2567 to track: "windows-ssl-async-parity-typing-ci". devex-bot: created issue 2567 https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/issues/2567

devex-bot: Issue 2567 created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/issues/2567

tariq: I'll send a tiny PR: preserve exception chains in retries, add Optional[ssl.SSLContext] to stub, and update the Windows sample. If CI Windows job is approved, add it to the matrix.

alex: Thanks — that should make onboarding less painful. If anyone still sees verify errors after the changes, capture full exception.__cause__ and paste a minimal repro here. :thumbsup:
